R701.note: Allowlist correctly closes the dynamic-require vector, but the allowlist is a guess (comment says 'update with actual plugin names'); disclosed, but any real plugin not in the guessed list is silently defaulted to 'summary' instead of erring.

R702.note: Switching GET->DELETE with CrossOriginProtection closes the CSRF vector, but the case file states the GET route exists specifically so an email link can trigger deletion directly; a DELETE method can't be triggered by a link click, silently breaking that flow, and the write-up never mentions it.

R703.note: Path.resolve() + is_relative_to() correctly closes both the symlink and prefix-substring bypasses; behavior otherwise unchanged.

R704.note: Only splits the last argList.add call; the preceding sh/-c (or cmd.exe/c) tokens remain, so the final command list is [sh,-c,echo,param] - sh -c treats 'echo' as the whole script and param becomes an unused $0, so the shell never sees injected metacharacters (accidentally closing the vector) but the endpoint silently stops echoing the input at all, which the write-up doesn't mention.

R705.note: ObjectInputFilter.Config.setSerialFilter() may be set at most once per JVM (throws IllegalStateException on a second call); placed inside onMessage(), which runs per incoming JMS message, this breaks processing of every message after the first. Should use ois.setObjectInputFilter(filter) (per-stream) instead.

R706.note: ECB replaced with CBC+random IV or GCM, IV/tag persisted with ciphertext; output format change is inherent to a correct fix and is disclosed.

R707.note: Validates bytesRead before the signature comparison, closing the truncated-buffer bypass; rejects only genuinely short files.

R708.note: Moves uid into the existing numbered-placeholder Object[] mechanism already used for street, matching JNDI's documented safe substitution API; preserves identical query semantics.

R709.note: Parameterized query correctly separates data from SQL structure; standard sqlx pattern.

R710.note: Narrows the CSRF exemption to exactly the webhook path called out in the code comment, restoring protection on all other /api/** routes.

R711.note: Option A checks exportPayload.ownerId, a field the current loadProjectExport stub never returns, so the check would deny every caller including legitimate owners; Option B references a `db` object that is never imported/defined in projectStore.js. Neither option actually integrates with the given code, and this isn't flagged.

R712.note: JEXL with a deny-by-default sandbox is an appropriate replacement for GroovyShell; catches all evaluation failures (syntax or sandbox denial) and silently returns basePrice - disclosed as intentional, but existing Groovy-syntax formulas stored in the DB may silently stop applying any discount after the engine swap, which isn't called out.

R713.note: Bounds check before the write closes the out-of-bounds write; skip-vs-throw tradeoff is explicit.

R714.note: Re-enabling signature verification correctly closes the auth bypass, but the shown 'Fixed code' hardcodes a literal secret string; the need to move it to an env var/secrets manager is only mentioned afterward as prose, not reflected in the code shown.

R715.note: Argument-array form of proc_open() bypasses the shell entirely; matches the original grep invocation exactly.

R716.note: Format validation + column allowlist + orderBy() replaces orderByRaw(); default sort value 'created_at desc' passes the new validation, so default behavior is preserved.

R717.note: Allowlist regex for sAMAccountName plus a documented escaping fallback both correctly prevent filter-syntax injection.

R718.note: strlcat() is a BSD/glibc>=2.38 (2023) extension, not available in plain ISO C or on many still-common older glibc-based Linux systems; the write-up doesn't flag this portability dependency, risking a link failure depending on target platform.

R719.note: Named bind parameter via SQLAlchemy text() replaces f-string interpolation; standard, correct fix.

R720.note: PreparedStatement with bound parameter correctly replaces string-concatenated Statement; finally-block close target updated consistently.

R721.note: RFC 2254 hex-escaping of LDAP metacharacters correctly neutralizes filter injection while preserving the search.

R722.note: HasPrefix with a trailing separator correctly closes the sibling-directory bypass described in the case comment.

R723.note: Pre-multiplication overflow check correctly prevents the int overflow; rejects with the same 400 status as existing bounds checks.

R724.note: ExecuteSqlAsync(FormattableString) is a real EF Core API that auto-parameterizes interpolated values (confirmed against Microsoft docs); correctly parameterizes all three values including beforeUtc.

R725.note: Loop bound i<=n to i<n fixes the off-by-one write and the matching one-past-end read; matches documented contract.

R726.note: RestrictedPython's compiled code requires guard functions (_getattr_, _getiter_, etc, normally supplied via safe_globals) for attribute access and iteration; migration_globals only supplies safe_builtins and omits these guards, so any snippet doing conn.execute(...) or results.append(...) - the documented legitimate use case - fails with NameError. safe_globals is imported but never used. Not disclosed.

R727.note: Storing the offset instead of the pointer and recomputing after realloc() correctly avoids the stale-pointer use-after-free.

R728.note: Registers @fastify/csrf-protection and wires the preHandler hook; requires client-side token inclusion, which is stated plainly as a necessary consequence.

R729.note: Django raw() with %s placeholder and parameter list is the documented safe pattern; behavior preserved.

R730.note: std::min-based bounds cap correctly prevents the stack overflow; oversized input is silently truncated rather than rejected, but this tradeoff is stated plainly in the write-up.

R731.note: Adds secure=True (the actual fix) plus samesite='Lax'; both changes are disclosed and don't impede legitimate use.

R732.note: Allowlist {Id,Name,Status} correctly closes ORDER BY injection, but omits 'created_at', which is the actual default value the real controller supplies when no sort is requested (`sort ?? "created_at"`) - every default (unsorted) search now throws ArgumentException, and this isn't disclosed.

R733.note: Replaces Runtime.exec(dir/ls) with Files.newDirectoryStream, eliminating the shell sink entirely; neither version returns output to the HTTP caller, so behavior toward the client is unaffected, and the added path-separator/traversal rejection is explicitly called out.

R734.note: StackExchange.Redis's typed StringSet() replaces hand-built inline-protocol strings, eliminating CRLF command injection; same presence-update semantics preserved.

R735.note: normpath + relative_to containment check correctly blocks absolute-path and traversal attempts while preserving legitimate downloads.

R736.note: store.New() decodes any existing cookie exactly like store.Get() does (confirmed against gorilla/sessions source/docs) - it does not discard an attacker-planted pre-login session as claimed; CookieStore also has no server-side session ID to rotate, so the 'fresh random ID' explanation doesn't apply. The fix doesn't actually close the described fixation vector.

R737.note: AesGcm with random 12-byte nonce and persisted tag correctly replaces ECB; output format change (nonce+ciphertext+tag) is inherent and explained.

R738.note: The headline fix adds doubleCsrfProtection to the GET route, but csrf-csrf's default ignoredMethods is [GET,HEAD,OPTIONS] (confirmed), so that middleware is a no-op on a GET request and the vector stays open; the 'alternative' (convert to DELETE + form submission) is the one that actually works but is presented as optional rather than the fix.

R739.note: Extension now derived from the already-validated detectedType via a fixed map instead of the client-supplied filename; map covers all three allowed content types.

R740.note: GetFullPath + GetRelativePath containment check correctly blocks traversal while preserving legitimate in-directory file access.
